messages:
maya: Quick follow-up from the continuous-batcher RFC — spotted a recurrent tail-latency pattern during tenant reshuffles in canary yesterday. Sharing notes and quick ideas for mitigation.
liam: Saw that in the graphs. 95/99 spikes line up with 'lease reacquire' events.
olivia: do we have a simple reproducer? logs or timeline?
sam: minimal repro attached in the canary run — short version: heavy coalescing + tenant move -> brief pause while kvcache pointers are reconciled. Logs: `WARN lease: reacquire 0.3s; batching_pause=320ms`
maya: exact. Most requests are fine, but when a tenant loses a slot we sometimes see a microburst of inflight batches that then contend on the packer, which triggers an internal stall.
liam: root cause hypothesis: when we preempt a slab, inflight windows are compacted and we drop KV locality assumptions, so kernels warmup + mutex contention = extra latency.
olivia: Proposed short-term fixes: (1) jitter lease expiration, (2) soft-drain (let small batches finish) before eviction, (3) backpressure signal to front-door to slow tiny requests. thoughts?
sam: ranking: (2) soft-drain easiest; (1) is low-risk but needs cross-node clock skew checks; (3) requires API client signal path which is heavier.
maya: agree. Soft-drain: let in-flight batches of size <= N finish; for >N we preempt. N=4?
liam: N=4 feels reasonable; we measured median batch size 3. Also add an opt-in flag on placement flow so Dedicated customers can keep aggressive preemptions.
olivia: can we land a guard in the enqueue path that rejects new joins to a slab marked for eviction, rather than forcefully compacting? sample patch:```
// pseudo
if (slab.marked_for_eviction && batch.size > soft_threshold) {
  return ENQUEUE_RETRY_LATER;
}
```
that avoids reshuffle thrash.
sam: +1 but need metrics: count of ENQUEUE_RETRY_LATER and a histogram of retry latency. Also a circuit breaker to fallback to immediate preempt after X retries.
maya: ops checklist if we roll: a) feature-flag rollout to canary b) +obs: `eviction.retries`, `eviction.soft_drain_ms`, `pack.lock_wait_ms` c) run 48h canary against reshuffle scenario.
liam: also add a small experiment: increase batch compact backoff from 50ms -> 200ms when eviction_rate > 1/s. That should smooth spikes.
olivia: edgecases: what if tenant is latency-sensitive (SLO-backed)? soft-drain could cause longer queuing for others. Need per-tenant policy: SLO==true => prefer immediate preempt + fallback to warm standby.
maya: agreed — expose `eviction_policy: soft|hard|standby` on tenant config. default soft for general-purpose.
sam: I'll open an RFC follow-up with action items + rollout plan and link the canary logs. ticket: INF-4123.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: canary/2026-03-21T14:10 (commit abc123)
liam: quick validation script I ran: `python experiments/reshuffle_probe.py --tenants 120 --workload mix` — baseline P99 dropped from 220ms -> 165ms with soft-drain + backoff. numbers look promising.
olivia: can we add a brief test in CI that simulates a slab eviction path? unit + integration harness would prevent regressions.
maya: yes, add both: unit to validate enqueue guard, integration to run short reshuffle scenario (30s). I'll own CI test.
sam: ok owners: maya (CI & rollout), liam (metrics + backoff tuning), olivia (per-tenant policy + config), sam (RFC doc + ticket). target: small-canary this week, wider rollout next week if green.
liam: one more: add an emergency escape hatch: `RUNTIME_DISABLE_SOFT_DRAIN=true` so we can instantly revert without code rollback.
maya: done. thanks all :thumbsup:
